subject: Math
prompt: Two nearby flagpoles are perpendicular to the ground, which is flat. One of these flagpoles is $18$ feet tall and has a shadow that is $6$ feet long. At the same time, the shadow of the other flagpole is $4$ feet long. How tall, in feet, is the other flagpole?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Each flagpole and its shadow can be modeled using a right triangle, where the height of the flagpole and the length of its shadow are the legs of the triangle. At a given point in time, the right triangles formed by two nearby flagpoles and their respective shadows will be similar. Therefore, if the height of the other flagpole is $x$, in feet, the value of $x$ can be calculated by solving the proportional relationship $\frac{18 \text{ feet tall}}{6 \text{ feet long}} = \frac{x \text{ feet tall}}{4 \text{ feet long}}$. This equation is equivalent to $\frac{18}{6} = \frac{x}{4}$, or $3 = \frac{x}{4}$. Multiplying each side of the equation $3 = \frac{x}{4}$ by $4$ yields $12 = x$. Therefore, the other flagpole is $12$ feet tall.
